state.startup_desc: FieldSense sells wireless soil-moisture sensors and a mobile irrigation scheduling app that helps small and mid-size farms cut water use without losing yield.
state.customer_profile: Owners of small and mid-size vegetable and orchard farms (20–500 ha) in dry regions that irrigate from metered wells or paid water sources.
state.customer_user: Farm managers and irrigation staff who check the app and run the irrigation system.
state.behaviour_actor: Whoever decides when and how much to irrigate on the farm (usually the farm manager, not the owner).
state.customer_value: Lower water and pumping costs with stable yields: every m³ of water the farm does not apply is also money saved.

Adoption chain.description: Wireless soil-moisture sensors feed a mobile app that generates daily irrigation recommendations calibrated to crop type and soil profile.
Adoption chain.assumption: Recommendations are accurate and trustworthy enough that farmers follow them instead of habitual watering schedules.

Adoption chain.description: 62 farms enrolled across the pilot region (up from 40 six months ago), averaging 3.2 sensors per farm.
Adoption chain.assumption: Enrolled farms are reasonably representative of typical smallholder operations in the region, not just early-adopter outliers.

Adoption chain.description: Pilot farmers report checking the app before irrigating and anecdotally watering less often.
Adoption chain.assumption: App engagement actually translates into reduced water applied, not just reduced perceived need to water.

Adoption chain.description: Reduced groundwater and surface-water withdrawal per irrigated hectare.
Adoption chain.assumption: Water savings are not offset by farmers expanding their irrigated area with the water they save (rebound effect).

state.weakest_links: The behavior-change assumption is the weakest link in the chain. We have solid enrollment numbers, but no water-meter data yet confirming that farmers actually reduce withdrawal rather than just feeling more informed — and we don't yet track whether saved water gets used to expand irrigated area instead.

Quality / reliability of adoption eviden.current_value: Self-reported survey (n=22 of 62): 71% say they irrigate less often; no metered verification yet
Quality / reliability of adoption eviden.target: Move to metered verification on a subset of farms
Quality / reliability of adoption eviden.pathway_link: Adoption chain → Outcomes: customer behavior change

Avoided physical harm per unit of adopti.target: Install water-flow meters on pilot farms' pumps
Avoided physical harm per unit of adopti.data_source: Not yet metered — currently estimated from published agronomic studies
Avoided physical harm per unit of adopti.pathway_link: Adoption chain → Impact: avoided environmental harm

Adoption rate of the solution.claim: 62 enrolled farms covering approximately 410 hectares as of this month.
Adoption rate of the solution.boundary: Farms with an active account and at least one installed sensor, as of the export date; excludes farms still onboarding.
Adoption rate of the solution.assumptions: Counts farms that are enrolled and have sensors installed; enrollment alone does not show that a farm actively uses the recommendations.

Quality / reliability of adoption eviden.claim: In a self-reported survey, 71% of responding pilot farmers (22 of 62 farms) say they irrigate less often since using FieldSense.
Quality / reliability of adoption eviden.baseline: Farmers' own recollection of how often they irrigated before using FieldSense
Quality / reliability of adoption eviden.sources: Self-reported survey of 22 of 62 enrolled farms
Quality / reliability of adoption eviden.boundary: 22 of 62 pilot farms that answered the 2026 mid-season survey; self-selected respondents.
Quality / reliability of adoption eviden.assumptions: This measures what farmers report, not how much water they use: irrigating less often can still mean the same or more water per irrigation. Social-desirability bias likely inflates positive answers.
Quality / reliability of adoption eviden.conditions: Would look different with a larger, randomly sampled survey, or with metered water use instead of self-report.

Avoided physical harm per unit of adopti.claim: Scenario: if pilot farms follow the recommendations through the 2027 season, water withdrawal per irrigated hectare could fall by up to 18% compared with the 2025 regional average. Not yet measured on FieldSense farms.
Avoided physical harm per unit of adopti.baseline: 2025 regional average water withdrawal per irrigated hectare (published statistics)
Avoided physical harm per unit of adopti.sources: Published agronomic studies of comparable sensor-guided irrigation systems in other regions
Avoided physical harm per unit of adopti.boundary: Scenario for the 2027 irrigation season: water applied per hectare on enrolled farms; excludes pumping energy and any expansion of irrigated area.
Avoided physical harm per unit of adopti.assumptions: Not yet based on FieldSense's own metered data; assumes pilot farms behave like the farms in the published studies.
Avoided physical harm per unit of adopti.conditions: Actual savings could be considerably lower if farmers under-trust recommendations during high-risk growth stages (e.g. flowering) and over-water as a precaution.

state.review_notes: Install water-flow meters on at least 10 pilot farms before the next review, to convert the core avoided-harm claim from projected to measured.
